explanations.Mo Farah: The British distance runner who won the Olympic 5,000m and 10,000m twice over.
explanations.Carl Lewis: The American sprinter and long jumper who won the Olympic 100 metres in 1984.
explanations.Usain Bolt: The Jamaican sprinter who won the Olympic 100 metres in a world record.
explanations.Rebecca Adlington: The British swimmer who won two freestyle golds at the 2008 Games.
explanations.Michael Phelps: The American swimmer who has won more Olympic golds than anyone.
explanations.Ian Thorpe: The Australian swimmer who won the 400m freestyle at his home Games in Sydney.
explanations.Chris Hoy: The track cyclist from Scotland who rode for Great Britain.
explanations.Greg LeMond: The American cyclist who was the first from his country to win the Tour de France.
explanations.Eddy Merckx: The Belgian rider counted as the most successful racer in cycling.

sources.excerpt: In a tactical, slow race, the gold medal was won by 0.32 seconds by reigning World champion Mo Farah of host Great Britain, completing a distance double having won the 10,000 metres a week earlier.
The event was won by Carl Lewis of the United States, that nation's first title after two Games of missing the podium (4th in 1976, boycotted in 1980).
The final was won by Jamaican Usain Bolt in a world record time of 9.69 seconds.

The son of David and Carol Hoy, Chris Hoy was born on 23 March 1976 and grew up in Murrayfield, Edinburgh.

editorNotes: Each of the nine competitors made their name in one of the three sports and represented one country, so every tile fits exactly one cell and the reading is forced. The cells that invite a second thought are the British ones. Mo Farah was born in Somalia, but he ran for Great Britain throughout his career, so he belongs in the British column and not in From elsewhere. Chris Hoy is Scottish and rode for Great Britain at the Olympics, so he is British here too. Greg LeMond is American, which keeps him out of the From elsewhere cell that Eddy Merckx, a Belgian, takes. Carl Lewis competed in the sprints and the long jump, both athletics, so he cannot slide into the swimming or cycling rows, and Michael Phelps, Ian Thorpe and Rebecca Adlington are swimmers only. Adam Peaty was considered for the British swimmer, but the encyclopaedia now files him under a changed surname and no plain sentence names him as written, so Rebecca Adlington takes that cell.
